en: The sampaguita, the Philippine national flower, is a jasmine species that blooms at night and releases a strong fragrance.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is a critically endangered forest predator endemic to the major islands of the Philippines.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces using ancient stone-walling techniques to prevent soil erosion on steep mountain slopes.
National hero Jose Rizal practiced ophthalmology in Dapitan, successfully performing cataract surgeries to restore his mother's eyesight.
The Philippine Constitution mandates that the President must be a natural-born citizen, at least forty years old, and able to read and write.
The Pahiyas Festival in Lucban, Quezon, decorates houses with kiping, which are leaf-shaped wafers made from ground rice and natural food coloring.
The Baybayin script, an ancient pre-colonial writing system used by early Filipinos, consists of seventeen basic syllabic characters representing consonants and vowels.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, from the balcony of his ancestral home in Kawit, Cavite.
National scientist Ramon Barba discovered that injecting mango trees with potassium nitrate solution safely induces flowering even during the dry season.
The traditional nipa hut, a symbol of Filipino bayanihan, uses bamboo and nipa palm leaves to create a naturally ventilated, earthquake-resistant structure.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea, requiring boat tours to explore.
Under the Philippine Bill of Rights, citizens are guaranteed the freedom of speech, freedom of the press, and the right to peaceful assembly.
